description: auto plugin hooks. SessionStart surfaces resumable runs (orphaned pulse chains + handoff pauses) so the operator can /auto-resume them — surfacing only, never auto-runs; for a programme's driving session it also reloads the rules in force, including after compaction. PreCompact flags each programme the compacting session drives, so its write verbs wait for `programme.py rules --ack`. Stop is the engine's OWN deliberate-stop guard: per the U9 spike (docs/research/native-goal-mechanism-spike.md) native /goal is a closed model-judged loop with no external predicate handoff, so auto ships its own thin Stop hook that BLOCKS via {"decision":"block"} (exit 0) while the I-1-fresh run-record predicate is unmet. PreToolUse adds the v0.6.0 advisor gate (KTD-4/5): on AskUserQuestion, on-pretooluse-askuser.sh DENIES + redirects to the advisor when a LIVE self-driven run owns this session (session_id == run_record.driving_session_id) — fail-OPEN; on-pretooluse-action.sh does not refuse destructive commands or pause a run for them: that check is off by default. On a Linear MCP tool call from a programme's driving session, the same hook denies a done or canceled state and a root-cause comment: proof comes from a worker or Shawn. The same PreToolUse hook refuses Write, Edit, MultiEdit and Bash calls that name the settings.local.json a programme permission proposal targets, or the personal behaviours folder or behaviours.json, for the driving session only. From a programme's driving session (gated on its lease file, not the repo walk), the AskUserQuestion PreToolUse hook also denies a call whose input pre-fills `answers`, and a PostToolUse hook journals each picker answer with a pick source record that resolves to origin `picked` only after a transcript check. The other hooks presence-gate (walk up for <repo>/.claude/auto or a programme lease) and all hooks always exit 0 (rel-001). Hook arrays merge additively, so this composes with cmux's entries and any native /goal. A further PreToolUse entry refuses programme write verbs, check-mergeable --pin and gh writes from a dispatched sub-agent of a programme's driving session (hook input carries agent_id), because a sub-agent inherits the PM's session id and the verbs' own guard cannot tell them apart. A PostToolUse hook on Agent and a SubagentStop hook, both async, record a driving session's background sub-agent as a worker item through add-item and set-waiting, and put the item back on the PM when the agent stops.
